# Interoperability and handoff

Use this file for a supplied design document, tool export or generated specification. `tokens.md`
owns value graphs and explicit conversion loss; `system-contracts.md` owns component seams. Keep
local format interpretation separate from tool access and target-runtime verification.

## Sections

- Dialect and acquisition — preserve source semantics and separate access from authority.
- Source-family intake — read authorized exports without adding native parsers or disclosure grants.
- Buildable handoff — carry components, states, acceptance and honest runtime limits.
- Portable role transfer — project canonical decisions into a fresh offline assignment.
- Constrained generated specifications — keep finite catalogs outside permission and business policy.

## Dialect and acquisition

A DESIGN.md filename is not a schema. Identify the declared dialect and authority before writing;
keep repository prose and unknown sections rather than forcing a fixed example's order. Brand-oriented
creative prose and token-bearing frontmatter can coexist but do not supply each other's missing
values. Extract candidates with source locations, units and uncertainty; no invented defaults,
automatic Google-format conversion or claim of native round-trip fidelity.

A design URL identifies a scope, not permission. Choose an authorized local export or already
available read path for the exact selection/file/library needed. Authentication, account/seat
eligibility, scope, file permission and tool support are independent gates; a denied endpoint does
not establish that every alternative is unavailable. Do not acquire credentials, connect an account
or invoke writes on this guide's authority. Service/API facts require current owner documentation.

Preserve collection and mode identity, aliases, original names/types/units, source revision and
unknown values before normalization. Unitless numbers do not become dimensions by name. Record
normalization collisions and unrepresentable semantics instead of silently flattening them. A
screenshot and structural export for different selections/revisions cannot be treated as one packet.
Archive inventory is not a native parser or semantic reconstruction.

## Source-family intake

Read `../shared/handoff/HANDOFF.md` → **Intake and authority** for the source-specific acquisition table.
Existing DESIGN.md and system specs retain units, aliases, modes, dialect and unknown sections. For
Figma, use an already-authorized read-only path for the exact selection or request matching visual,
token/style and state exports. PSD needs PNG/PDF plus text specs; AI needs PDF/SVG/PNG plus master
values; INDD needs PDF/style specs, optionally owner-exported font-free IDML inspected only with an
existing safe reader. Screenshots establish observed appearance, not hidden behavior or font identity.
No native parser, connector activation, archive extraction or Adobe font-file access is added.

Attribute actual inspected scope/revision and authority in `sources[].intake`; keep unread/partial/
unavailable and inferred material distinct. Sharing needs separate approval of selected content and
recipient boundary. A public link or asset-use grant is not permission to disclose it to a model.
Conflicts remain explicit under the existing authority order. A new system task leaves its starting
`context.design` unchanged; later tasks inherit the adopted system normally.

## Buildable handoff

Reuse the existing project record: name the task/surface, source scope and revision, observed versus
inferred intent, protected decisions, intended changes, unresolved owner decisions and acceptance.
Specify reading/focus order, responsive transformations, meaningful states, public component events,
semantics, copy/asset approval and interrupted/recovery behavior—not only measurements. Cross-target
seams need their actual behavior owner. Read-only diagnosis has no repair authority.

Map the packet to maintained components before generating code. A component match, extracted token
or valid generated element proves neither interactions nor fidelity. Name exactly which route/state,
viewport, input, theme/locale and runtime must be exercised; preserve unverified behaviors as open
work, not assumed passes. `ulm-release` owns the actual gate, not this handoff description.

## Portable role transfer

Read `../shared/handoff/HANDOFF.md` → **Projection annotations**, **Export**, and **Return and freshness**.
`lapis-design handoff export --plan <plan> --scope <scope> --role <role>` resolves an explicitly shareable
scope for design-head, implementer or reviewer, without network or receiver skill installation.
The 32 KiB UTF-8 cap blocks an oversized scope instead of truncating decisions, rights or acceptance.
Returns are proposals bound to the original content hashes; `handoff check` is read-only and rejects
stale inputs. The coordinator reconciles/approves locally and reruns actual checks. No remote claim
is imported as a local approval, critic, render, behavior or release pass.

## Constrained generated specifications

A finite catalog is a spec-to-component boundary, not a complete design system or permission layer.
Keep canonical tokens and business policy outside model-generated markup. Expose meaningful bounded
roles, not arbitrary HTML, styles, URLs or handlers. Separate structural graph checks, application
prop/schema and resource bounds, and runtime/server authorization. Test missing/cyclic references,
expansion/depth/size and actual props under the installed implementation rather than assuming an
SDK envelope validates every value.

Visibility is not access control, registered actions are not user permission, and partial streamed
patches are not a confirmed transaction. Keep private/server-only data out of client rendering state.
Validate identity, resource scope and consequential actions at the existing authoritative boundary;
retain the last valid usable view and a real failure state when a candidate or stream is invalid.
No package, renderer, backend policy or validation subsystem is added by this reference.
